definitions.explanation: One of the five major styles of Chinese/Japanese calligraphy. A flowing style between the rigid block script and the highly abbreviated cursive script, commonly used in everyday handwriting.

examples.japanese: {行書|ぎょうしょ}で{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}く。
examples.english: To write one's name in semi-cursive script.

examples.japanese: {行書|ぎょうしょ}は{楷書|かいしょ}より{速|はや}く{書|か}ける。
examples.english: Semi-cursive script can be written faster than block script.

examples.japanese: {書道|しょどう}{教室|きょうしつ}で{楷書|かいしょ}の{次|つぎ}に{行書|ぎょうしょ}を{習|なら}った。
examples.english: In calligraphy class, I learned semi-cursive script after block script.

notes: Composed of {行|ぎょう} (go, move, flow) + {書|しょ} (writing, script). One of the five traditional script styles ({五体|ごたい}): {篆書|てんしょ} (seal script), {隷書|れいしょ} (clerical script), {楷書|かいしょ} (block/regular script), {行書|ぎょうしょ} (semi-cursive), and {草書|そうしょ} (cursive). {行書|ぎょうしょ} is considered the most practical for everyday use — it simplifies strokes of {楷書|かいしょ} while remaining readable, unlike the highly abbreviated {草書|そうしょ}. Japanese handwriting naturally tends toward {行書|ぎょうしょ} when writing quickly.
